sections.html: Accents in French are not decoration. They change pronunciation and sometimes meaning. There are five accent marks.

sections.heading: 1. Accent aigu ( ´ ) — only on **é**
sections.html:
• Sound: a closed "ay", like the start of "day" without the glide.
  • Very common in past participles and nouns.
  • Examples: été (summer / been), café, parlé (spoken), étudiant (student).

sections.heading: 2. Accent grave ( ` ) — on **è**, **à**, **ù**
sections.html:
• è = open "eh", like "bed": mère (mother), père (father), très (very).
  • à and ù don't change the sound. They distinguish words:
  • a (has) vs à (to/at): Il a un chien. / Il va à Paris.
  • ou (or) vs où (where): Thé ou café ? / Où es-tu ?
  • la (the) vs là (there).

sections.heading: 3. Accent circonflexe ( ^ ) — on **â, ê, î, ô, û**
sections.html:
• Often marks a letter s that disappeared from older French. Compare with English: forêt = forest, hôpital = hospital, fête = feast, île = isle.
  • ê sounds like è (open "eh"): tête (head), fenêtre (window).
  • ô is a closed "oh": hôtel, côte.
  • It sometimes distinguishes words: sur (on) vs sûr (sure); du (some) vs dû (owed).

sections.heading: 4. Tréma ( ¨ ) — on **ë, ï, ü**
sections.html:
• Tells you to pronounce the vowel separately from the one before it.
  • Noël (No-el, not "nole"), naïf (na-eef), maïs (corn: ma-ees), Haïti.

sections.heading: 5. Cédille ( ¸ ) — only on **ç**
sections.html:
• Makes c sound like s before a, o, u (where it would otherwise be "k").
  • français, garçon (boy), reçu (received). (More in Subject 3.)

sections.heading: Summary table
sections.html:
Mark Letters Effect Example
aigu é closed "ay" été
grave è, à, ù è = open "eh"; à/ù distinguish words mère, à, où
circonflexe â ê î ô û ê = "eh"; often a lost s forêt
tréma ë ï ü pronounce vowel separately Noël
cédille ç c = "s" garçon

Typing tip: On a phone, press and hold a letter to see its accented versions.

exercises.prompt: Choose *a* or *à*: (a) Elle ___ vingt ans. (b) Je vais ___ l'école.
Choose *ou* or *où*: (a) ___ habites-tu ? (b) Tu veux du thé ___ du café ?
Which English word is hidden in: *forêt*, *hôpital*, *bête*, *pâte*?

exercises.answer: "no-el" — the tréma tells you to pronounce ë separately.

exercises.prompt: Is the **e** in *mère* pronounced like "ay" or "eh"?
